column3: That's no ordinary tree.\nLook at the arms.\nThe face. A man...?{end_wait}

Welcome to Bilibin.
Ignore the tree out front.
Everyone else does.{page_break}Warriors have been sent
to Kolima. Don't ask how
many have come back.{end_wait}
A big group crossed the\nGoma Range. Heading for\nImil, last I heard.{end_wait}
You saw the tree at the\nentrance, didn't you?{end_now}
Lord McCoy hasn't left\nhis palace since the\nincident. He's terrified.{end_wait}
Ever tried heading\nsoutheast from here?{end_now}
The Kolima road is shut.\nLord McCoy's orders.\nNo one gets through.{end_wait}

Ever since that man
turned into a tree,
nobody sleeps well.{page_break}Folks avoid the town
gate. Some swear the
tree whispers at night.{end_wait}

Is it true a mountain
blew itself apart beyond
the Goma Range?{page_break}The sky burned red all
night. It was beautiful,
and I feel guilty for it.{end_wait}

There's a tower at Imil's
far tip. Folks say gods
built it.{page_break}The locals call it the
lighthouse. No one I
know has seen inside.{end_wait}

Something{pause_20_skippable} changed
when that mountain blew.{page_break}Now there are things in
every forest and cave.
Things that hunt.{end_wait}
My lumber from Kolima\nnever arrived. Nobody\nfrom Kolima did,{pause_20_skippable} after.{end_wait}
You've seen the barricade\nwe put up on the Kolima\nroad?{end_now}
So you're saying this\nis my fault?{end_now}
Rotten luck, coming to\nBilibin now. We're not\nat our best.{end_wait}
Imil? In winter? Are you\nout of your minds?{end_wait}

This is Lady McCoy's
doing, plain and simple.{page_break}All she wanted was a
palace. Look what that
cost us.{end_wait}

When a lord hides, the
rest of us start to
worry.{page_break}Can we still count on
him? I'm not sure
anymore.{end_wait}
Who let these children\nin here?{end_wait}
After last time, no one\nwill dare go after it\nagain.{end_wait}

He begged for help while
he changed. We all just
stood and watched.{page_break}Is that what grown-ups
are? Cowards?{end_wait}
I keep thinking about\nthat red sky.\nI want to see it again.{end_wait}
Only great Adepts may\nenter Imil's lighthouse.\nThe rest are turned away.{end_wait}

That blast was an omen.
Something terrible is
coming.{page_break}I can feel it. I'm
so scared.{end_wait}

If this keeps up, maybe
we should stop building
that palace.{page_break}The gods are telling us
something.{end_wait}

I'm glad I never knew
Kolima was tied up in
this...{page_break}If I had, I'd never have
taken the job. Not for
any price.{end_wait}

If that sacred tree
caused all this,
then cut it down!{page_break}Burn it, if we have to.
End it.{end_wait}

That tree at the gate was
a man. The sacred tree
cursed him.{page_break}It's because McCoy had
the forest cut down for
his wife's palace.{end_wait}
McCoy cut down the trees\nto build his wife a\nbigger, grander palace.{end_wait}

This is Lord McCoy's
fault. But who here would
say it to his face?{page_break}He's our lord. We keep
our mouths shut.{end_wait}

Lady McCoy... I'd give
anything to be her.{page_break}Will I ever live in a
palace of my own? Hah.
Not in this life.{end_wait}
Snow is already piling up\nin Imil, and it's freezing.{page_break}If I were you, I'd wait for\nspring. People die there.{end_wait}
We hardly ever get snow\nin Bilibin.{end_wait}
When spring comes, I'm\ngoing to see that angel\n{actor_name:4} again.{end_wait}
Living in a snowbound\ntown must be hard.{page_break}I think I'll stay right\nhere, where it's warm.{end_wait}
Has anyone heard from\nKolima? I've been sick\nwith worry.{end_wait}
I know that man by the\ngate. I'd know those\nclothes anywhere.{end_wait}
I can't believe all of\nKolima is trees now.\nBut what if it is?{end_wait}

He was laughing just a
day before. Then he was
bark and root.{page_break}What if it happens to
me? Just like that?{end_wait}

Long ago, the Imil
lighthouse held the Water
of Hermes.{page_break}They say it could heal
any wound. Any wound at
all.{end_wait}

But not even Hermes'
water can turn back time.{page_break}I'd give my last coin
for a potion to make me
young again.{end_wait}
Could the Water of Hermes\nsave a man who turned\ninto a tree?{end_wait}
The Water of Hermes is\nlong gone.{page_break}Nothing good lasts.\nThat's just how it is.{end_wait}
There was a healer in\nVale. A gifted one.\nHe's gone now.{end_wait}
We'll never see a healer\nlike him again. The\nworld's poorer for it.{end_wait}
Have you ever heard of\nthe ocean?{end_now}
I'd love to see what's\nbeyond this world.\nIf only I were younger.{end_wait}
You look like you've seen\ntrouble. Plenty of it.{page_break}Lord McCoy could use\nsomeone like you.{end_wait}
Only a brave man\nwould walk into a place\nlike that.{end_wait}
A curse on Kolima...\nWhere does it end?{end_wait}
Kolima's cut off. Don't\nbother trying.{end_wait}

I was born in Kolima.
I can't stop thinking
about my family.{page_break}My hands shake. I can't
focus on the cooking.{end_wait}
Hey, Chef! Are you going\nto cook, or what?{page_break}The customers are\nwaiting!{end_wait}
Cook something already!{end_wait}

We came because Lord
McCoy was building a
palace for his wife.{page_break}Did they stop because
of the curse?{end_wait}
That big tree deep in\nthe forest. Something's\nwrong with it.{end_wait}
Do you think a tree\nspirit can curse a man?{end_now}
I can't wait for today's\nspecial! Smells great.{end_wait}
I went to Lord McCoy for\nwork...{page_break}But I'm too scared to\ntake the job alone.{end_wait}

Old songs say ancient
trees can grow strange
powers.{page_break}Maybe that power is what
caused{pause_20_skippable} the {text_effect:4}curse{reset_text_style}.{end_wait}
I don't believe a tree\ncan curse anyone.{end_wait}

Travelers heading east are
stuck until the road
reopens.{page_break}Fine by me. They have
to sleep somewhere.{end_wait}
Mother... Father... I\nhope you're safe.{page_break}I'd run home right now\nif I could.{end_wait}
Should I forget I'm the\nnew one and just start\ncooking?{end_wait}
I've heard every\ncomplaint I can stand!{end_wait}

Argh! I could scream,
I'm so hungry!{page_break}But I have to smile.
Being a businessman
is hard.{end_wait}

I came to Bilibin to sell
furniture. All I got was{page_break}a palace nobody's
building and a kitchen
that won't feed me.{end_wait}
Now I see why they call\nthe big tree in Kolima\nForest sacred.{end_wait}
I don't care who does it.\nJust lift this curse!{end_wait}
Is it ready yet? I'm\nstarving.{end_wait}
All these stories are\nstarting to scare me.{end_wait}
They say a spirit named\nTret lives inside the\nholy tree.{end_wait}
Lord McCoy is so shaken\nby the curse that he\ncan't eat.{end_wait}

The lord only sees brave,
mighty warriors.{page_break}You don't look the part.
Do you think you can do
the job?{end_now}
Lord McCoy is a hard\nman. Watch what you say\naround him.{end_wait}
The master's temper is\nshort. Don't keep him\nwaiting.{end_wait}
Nobody believed it could\nhappen. Then they all\nturned to wood.{end_wait}
Is there no one who can\nhelp us?{end_wait}
Lord McCoy won't hire\nsome scrawny kids.{end_wait}
To see Lord McCoy,\nfollow the red carpet.{end_wait}
Don't offend Lord McCoy.\nI'm warning you.{end_wait}
You'd really go into\nKolima Forest?{end_now}
I always said the old\ntree in Kolima Forest\nshould be left alone.{end_wait}
This is Lady McCoy's\nroom. Touch nothing.{end_wait}
How many times must I\ntell them? Why won't they\nleave me be?{end_wait}

Children shouldn't be
allowed in the palace!{page_break}If they break an urn,
I'm the one who gets
the blame!{end_wait}
Sending children into\nKolima Forest?{page_break}Do they want more\npeople cursed?{end_wait}

I should've kept quiet
when they planned the
new palace.{page_break}Maybe I'm the reason
they cut down the
holy tree...{end_wait}
The nerve! Walking into\nthe palace unescorted!{end_wait}

Milady was famous for her
beauty, far and wide.{page_break}That's why milord will
pay any price to please
her.{end_wait}
Someday I'll sleep in a\nsilk nightgown like this.{end_wait}
Will anyone ever make my\ndreams come true, like\nmilady's did?{end_wait}
Oh no. A hole in the\nnightgown. Milady will\nbe furious!{end_wait}

You can see Kolima from
here.{page_break}On sunny days, Lord
McCoy came to admire
the view.{end_wait}
The curse hasn't reached\nBilibin yet.\nNot yet.{end_wait}
Lord McCoy hasn't been\nhere in a long while.{page_break}It's the curse. What\nelse would keep him away?{end_wait}

Kolima Forest used to be
so green. After they cut
the holy tree,{page_break}everything turned brown.
Is the forest dying...?{end_wait}

Well? These are Bilibin's
great treasures.{page_break}Whoever ends the curse
may claim them as his
own.{end_wait}
We're giving our\ntreasure to these\nweaklings?{end_wait}
What use is treasure to\na man who's turned to\nwood?{end_wait}
Bah! Yeh're too young.\nYeh cannae handle this.{end_wait}
Are you serious,\n{actor_name:1}? That didn't\nbother you at all?{end_now}
Don't let him get to you.{page_break}We'll prove we can\nhandle this job, whatever\nit is.{end_wait}
Hey! No job done,\nno reward!{end_wait}
That's all I know.\nDon't ask again.{end_wait}
Shame. Come back when\nyou've grown a bit.{end_wait}

There's nothing more to
discuss!{page_break}Send them away. I don't
care how many times they
come back!{end_wait}
It's hard, being that\nyoung.{page_break}They dinnae ken what\nit means to be afraid.{end_wait}

That barricade's shoddy.
We built it in a rush.{page_break}The hinges are noisy
and weak. A good push
might break them.{end_wait}
I can't believe they let\nyou go. You're too young!{end_wait}
Even frozen Imil must\nfeel warm with {actor_name:4}\nthere.{end_wait}
A tree... shaped like\na person. Disturbing.{end_wait}
I was a tree for a\nwhile. Can you believe\nthat?{end_now}
Welcome to Bilibin.{pause_20_skippable}\nWe'll forget this curse\nbusiness soon enough.{end_wait}
The travelers from Imil?\nThey crossed the river.{end_wait}

The tree by the gate?
It's a man again.{page_break}Thank the gods. I
thought it'd stay that
way forever.{end_wait}

I saw Lord McCoy walking
the streets today,
first time in ages.{page_break}He must be relieved
the curse is broken.{end_wait}
The barricade on the\nKolima road is open\nagain, I hear.{end_wait}
Those three kids\ndisappeared in the middle\nof all that trouble.{end_wait}

Three young warriors
broke the curse.{page_break}Say... you wouldn't be
those warriors, would
you?{end_now}
McCoy's men say they saw\nthe ones who saved us.{end_wait}
Ever been to Imil, up\nnorth?{end_now}
